## Workflow
- Invoice fixtures under tests/fixtures/invoices/ are the ground truth for payload shapes [seed].
- One route per resource; handlers stay thin, domain logic lives in src/domain/ [note 0].
- Use zod 3 schemas with .strict() for all payload validation; unknown keys must be rejected [note 5].
- Use pino for structured logging: JSON lines to stdout, one logger instance per module [note 3].

## Known pitfalls
- Prefer standard library functions over hand-rolled logic [note 2].
- Express error handler maps zod 3 .flatten() output to 400 responses for validation failures; 500 for all other errors [note 1].
- Configure pino redaction options with standard paths to keep card numbers out of logs [note 2].
- For outbound HTTP calls, use axios with interceptors: retry logic in response interceptor, auth header injection in request interceptor [note 7].
- Enforce alphabetical import sorting via ESLint; this catches merge conflicts early [note 4].

## Task playbooks
- To add a new payload type (e.g., credit-note): mirror the existing invoice zod schema structure, ensuring .strict() and clean flattening in the error handler [note 1].
- To integrate a new external provider: implement the client using axios interceptors for retry and auth; do not use plain fetch [note 7].
